title: Lab sprint playbook: integrations, cost gates, and rollback procedures
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint playbook for short-run customer lab engagements that include multiple third-party integrations, strict cost targets, and a defined rollback plan. Goal is to get a production-feasible end-to-end demo (API + infra + monitoring) within 3 weeks, with clear acceptance criteria and an explicit cost-gate before scaling.

Context / when to use this: 
- Customer asks for a multi-system pilot (Redwood hosted inference + customer DB + 3rd-party search/embeddings)
- Need a repeatable ops-friendly lab cadence to sign off on viability before sales commit to Dedicated/Private

High-level constraints / assumptions:
- Use Redwood hosted API for model serving unless the customer requires VPC; switch path documented below.
- Budget cap: $2,500 cloud inference spend for the lab (+ customer-provided infra credits). If projected > cap, trigger cost gate review.
- Security: no sensitive PII in test prompts unless approved and KMS is configured.
- SRE on-call for lab window: Owen Murphy (primary) / Ethan Park (secondary).

Sprint timeline (3 weeks):
Week 0 (pre-sprint, 3–5 days):
- Kickoff + scoping call notes + data checklist (owner: Maya) — due day -3
- Provision lab environment (temporary project in org, API keys, role-scoped credentials) (owner: Lina) — due day -2
- Integration smoke tests (customer DB read-only, search index connection) (owner: Priya) — due day -1

Week 1 (day 1–5):
- Workshop day 1: architecture walkthrough, success metrics, and demo scenario scripting (owner: Maya)
- Deliverable: Workshop notes, annotated demo script, file of test prompts
- Tasks: implement Redwood API client + sample pipeline, basic auth and error-handling, run 100 sample calls to verify latency distribution (owner: Ethan)

Week 2 (day 6–12):
- Integrations ramp: embeds pipeline wired to search, KV cache proof-of-concept, prefix caching config (owner: Priya)
- Metrics plumbing: basic tracing + cost estimator enabled, token-level sampling to estimate per-call spend (owner: Lina)
- Mid-sprint check: internal demo for SE lead and SRE; record checklist items (owner: Maya)

Week 3 (day 13–18):
- Harden demo: graceful fallbacks, retry/backoff, and canary route to smaller model variant for cost emergencies (owner: Ethan)
- Acceptance testing: run acceptance harness (scripted golden prompts vs expected outputs), record quality regressions and performance targets (owner: Maya)
- Final customer dry-run + handoff folder (owner: Priya)

Post-sprint (day 19–21):
- Decision gate meeting: present cost/time/performance, recommend next step (Dedicated commitment, extended pilot, or close) (presenter: Maya)
- Close tasks: scrub temporary keys, snapshot configs, add runbook to Confluence (owner: Lina)

Task tracker (short form; expand in Jira):
- LAB-01: Kickoff + scope doc (Maya) — created with action items and open questions.
- LAB-02: Env provisioning + API creds (Lina) — include expiration 30d, tags: pilot/customer-<name>
- LAB-03: DB + search connectors (Priya) — test vectors list + sample rows
- LAB-04: Redwood client integration + perf harness (Ethan) — scripts to replay 1k requests at 5 rps
- LAB-05: Cost estimator and alerting (Lina) — cloud spend mail-to + Slack alert at 70% cap
- LAB-06: Rollback runbook + fallback routing (Ethan/Owen) — documented manual and automated steps
- LAB-07: Acceptance harness + golden set (Maya) — pass threshold: 85% match on 200 prompt set
- LAB-08: Customer dry-run + feedback capture (Priya) — meeting recording + annotated notes

Acceptance criteria (must ALL be satisfied for green):
- Functional: demo scenario completes end-to-end with no fatal errors in 95% runs
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 750ms for primary route (with documented sequence length)
- Cost: projected 30-day equivalent cost <= 3x lab spend (ties into cost-gate) and immediate lab spend within $2,500 cap
- Quality: model outputs meet golden set threshold (85% fuzz-match) or have documented mitigations (re-ranker / prompt revisions)
- Security/compliance: no unapproved PII in logs; keys rotated and audit logged

Cost gate workflow:
- Trigger: projected run rate > $2,500 (estimate from token sampling + expected throughput).
- Immediate actions: throttle traffic, switch to smaller model variant, enable caching and reduce max tokens, pause non-essential experiments.
- Review board (within 24h): SE lead (Maya), SRE (Owen), Solutions Architect (Lina), Customer Success manager — decision to continue, pause, or require prepayment.

Rollback / emergency procedures (short):
- Immediate stop: disable lab API keys -> block outgoing traffic from lab project -> post a Slack /channel with incident tag.
- Partial rollback: switch route to cold variant (smaller model) via routing policy, set reduced max tokens, enable strict batching limits.
- Full rollback: fall back to a recorded canned-response demo (stored artifacts/canned-demo.tar.gz) for the customer to keep the demo while further investigation occurs.
- Post-incident: create RCA within 3 business days and link to Jira task.

Monitoring & observability checklist:
- Token-level meters enabled and sampled (owner: Lina)
- Per-route latency dashboard (redwood/console route: /pilot/<customer>) (owner: Ethan)
- Error rate and timeout alert > 1% triggers PagerDuty to SRE on-call (Owen)
- Cost spike alerting to trial-monitoring slack channel at 70% and 90% of budget

Workshop facilitation notes (for the initial day):
- Duration: 90 minutes (architectural review + demo script + success metrics)
- Attendees: customer engineering lead, solutions engineer, SRE rep, product PM (optional)
- Pre-reads: short prioritized list of integration endpoints and a sample dataset (send 48h before)
- Activities: map happy path, identify failure modes, and list fallback options. Capture open decisions inline and assign owners.

Decision log (live):
- 2025-10-21: Agreed to use hosted Redwood API for initial lab (Maya)
- 2025-10-22: Customer requested document-level PII redaction; KMS required before production (action: Lina)
- 2025-10-24: Cost cap agreed at $2,500; automatic throttling at 70% (action: Ethan)

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Confirm whether the customer will provide an embeddings index or we build one (owner: Priya)
- Add automated post-demo survey to capture qualitative acceptance signals (owner: Maya)
- Validate expected sequence length distribution with customer (owner: Ethan)

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider a lightweight feature flag in client to switch caching on/off per route for experiments.
- If the lab proves the workload is latency-sensitive but stable, prepare a cost/throughput estimate for Dedicated with 95th percentile SLOs.

Files to attach to Confluence when finalizing: 
- runbook.md (step-by-step provisioning & teardown)
- acceptance-harness.zip (scripts + golden sets)
- cost-model.csv (token sampling + extrapolation)
- workshop-notes.pdf (annotated meeting notes)

If you want a quick checklist view for the kickoff meeting: 
1) Confirm contact list + roles.
2) Verify 48h pre-read delivery.
3) Provision lab project and keys with 30d expiry.
4) Run integration smoke tests.
5) Baseline token and latency samples.
6) Schedule mid-sprint internal demo.
7) Prepare rollback canned responses.

-- end of playbook (working draft)

Working draft: expect this doc to be iterated in the sprint; capture changes in the decision log above.
